limitations: This document pools every comment collected across the whole 2021-2026 effort into a single analysis: 9,697 unique comments (4,541 Facebook, 5,156 Instagram) spanning 54 months from May 2021 to August 2026.

It is not the sum of the six March-November reports. Those windows exclude December, January and February; this pool includes them. 392 of the 895 complaints here - 44 percent - fall outside the six windows. That single difference is why snow and storm response leads this ranking but barely registers in the seasonal reports.

Coverage is uneven across the span. Instagram's public feed could not be paged back past March 2023, so 2021 and 2022 are Facebook-only. Facebook history was gathered as date-bounded slices rather than an exhaustive crawl, so each year is a sample of that year rather than every post published in it.

Volume rises steeply toward the present: 28 complaints are dated 2021 against 541 dated 2026. Recent years therefore dominate this pooled ranking. For a like-for-like read across years, use the six period reports, where each period is normalised to its own share.

Facebook comments were pulled from the most-commented posts in each window. Heavily discussed posts are over-represented on purpose - that is where grievances collect - so these shares describe the complaint conversation, not the average post.
Instagram contributes the comments returned alongside each post, a broader but shallower slice than Facebook.
Emoji-only, tag-only and one-word reactions are counted in the total collected but excluded from the base used for the complaint rate, since they express no grievance either way.
Comments posted by official city accounts are excluded, as the scrapers surface them alongside residents' replies.
A category can rank low simply because the city rarely posted about it. Treat the ranking as a measure of the conversation the city's own posts invited, not a census of civic opinion.
